⚠️ CORRECTED — DO NOT RE-QUOTE THE ORIGINAL. This row read: 'Three pre-spawn records for this session were described as written and landed on NO REF — an MI-15 recurrence.' THAT WAS TRUE WHEN MEASURED (~2026-09-10T21:40Z, git log --all -S over every ref: the registry key pending-20260910T213243Z, the object WO-20260910-DISPOSITION-THE-34-UNDISPOSITIONED-AUTOMATION-PRS-AND, and an ops-lane spawn-exception block were all absent) AND IT IS NOW FALSE. All three landed in #11736 (04151f4dd) at ~21:5xZ, complete and correct — main's pending row already carried this session's id and the right object, and main's exception file already carried a full ops-lane block. IT IS NOT AN MI-15 RECURRENCE AND MUST NOT BE FILED AS ONE; the manager wrote every record. WHAT SURVIVES IS NARROWER AND STILL REAL: registration is NOT ATOMIC WITH THE SPAWN, so a session that starts before its own pre-spawn PR merges will correctly measure its records as absent and may then duplicate them. This session did exactly that — it authored a second object (WO-20260910-DISPOSITION-THE-OPEN-AUTOMATION-PRS-RESCUE-THE) and a second exception block, then DELETED BOTH on discovering main's, adopting main's records wholesale. The cost was a duplicate object briefly existing and a three-way merge conflict; the fix is for the spawn prompt to name the PR that carries the records, so a cold session can tell 'not written' from 'not landed yet'.
